exposure: Presence of Clostridium innocuum, Cl. Perfringens, Cl. difficile, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, and Staphylococcus aureus in the gut
cohort: 52 SIDS infants and 102 age-matched live comparison infants
finding: SIDS babies had a significantly higher prevalence of gut colonization with Cl. difficile, Cl. innocuum, and B. thetaiotaomicron compared to healthy infants, suggesting a potential role of these bacteria in SIDS pathogenesis.
mod_finding: Infants born via mode of delivery other than vaginal delivery had altered gut microflora, making them more susceptible to infection and possibly sudden infant death syndrome.
